title: Scorch
description: A stack of real photographic prints, an alpine valley, a wildflower meadow, light beams at night, a man reading in a field, a visitor over the daisies, a clock tower and a figure on the wires, each with its own dark areas as the fuel. Press to burn and drag to draw the flame: the print hangs from its top edge, so the moment a piece is cut free it drops away on its own as a curling 3D fragment while the rest stays put and keeps burning, and the next photo takes over only once the last of the print has fallen.
intent: A heat-and-fuel burn sim on photographic prints where pale areas barely smoulder and dark areas burn like a fuse, and anything you cut free of the top edge falls away on its own.

changelog.summary:
Fixed the root cause of presses getting stuck: the hold-to-ignite check looked up the pointer by its string source id in a map keyed by numeric pointerId, so every hold after the self-lit intro filled its ring and then silently did nothing
Every press now gets its own fire id, so a new burn no longer deletes the one you lit a moment before
Holding keeps feeding the fire for up to 9s and slowly widens it, so pale paper and leftover islands can always be burnt through by hand instead of the source dying after 1.4s
Presses during a burn-through or the opening pre-sim are queued and light on the next sheet instead of being refused, and a finger still held when a sheet burns through carries its flame onto the cover underneath
If ignition is not possible yet the ring re-charges and retries while you hold, rather than going dead until you lift
Pointer bookkeeping is released on pointerup, cancel, lost capture, window blur and a repeated pointerdown, so a missed pointerup can no longer leave the plate stuck in a pressed or dragging state
Touch and pen get a 12px hold slop (mouse stays 6px), so a slightly wobbly finger still lights instead of turning into a drag
Up to 8 fires burn at once, up from 4
A sheet that has gone cold after a real burn (over 55% burnt, no heat, no live fire, nobody pressing) for 1.2s now finishes itself and rolls over to the next cover, so pale covers no longer strand you once their ink is gone
A held flame no longer dies under a still finger after 9s; it burns for as long as you hold, still capped in width
A press during a burn-through or the opening pre-sim keeps its ring charged and only whooshes, buzzes and bursts once the fire actually lights on the next sheet; lifting before then cancels it cleanly
Douse (Esc or the button) re-arms any finger still held: its ring recharges after the douse and it relights in place instead of going dead until you lift
Unmounting or re-running the pointer setup now ends every live pointer and keyboard fire first, so the wind, pressed state and frame loop can no longer be left running
Held burns get a ragged, fibre-led edge in the sim so long holds char organically instead of punching round cigarette holes

The pointer is now the flame: moving over the cover heats and burns along the path with no press or hold, and on touch, dragging burns
The flame is a moving heat stroke swept between frames, so fast moves leave no gaps, and how long it dwells sets the burn: a quick flick only toasts paper, an ordinary sweep lights darker ink, and a slow pass or a pause chars through bare paper
Holding the button (or a finger down) stokes the flame hotter and wider and keeps widening it while held, replacing the old hold-to-ignite ring
A still mouse dims to an ember after 4s so a parked cursor stops burning and the frame loop can rest, and any movement relights it instantly
The custom cursor stays visible as the flame, grows while stoked and shrinks to an ember when idle
Once 36% of the sheet has burnt (or it sits cold past 24% for 1.6s, or you press Next sheet) it breaks along ragged, noise-warped cracks into about 36 charred pieces instead of dissolving
Cracks flash with ember and darken to a char lip, then pieces nearest the burn lift first, rising on decaying heat with a gentle flutter, rock and spin before gravity wins and they tumble, some flipping to show the plain toasted paper back, and fall away
Pieces keep the exact look of the sheet at the moment it broke, and their ember edges and warm glow cool as they fly
The next cover is installed the instant the sheet breaks, so the flame keeps burning the new cover underneath the falling pieces with no dead time
The old sheet’s soot and ember light fade off the new cover over 1.6s so the hand-off has no pop
Moving the flame under falling pieces gives them an updraft and pushes them along, so you can keep them aloft
The canvas now bleeds past the cover so pieces can rise above it and fall below it over the page, with soft edges; the cover keeps its rounded corners and nothing outside it takes clicks
Pieces are instanced GPU quads drawn in one call from a per-frame typed buffer, with no React state; the retired sim state is swapped rather than copied, and every new buffer and texture is disposed
Reduced motion fades the pieces in place instead of flying them
Copy updated to say the pointer is the flame

Burning now happens only while pressed: a click lights a spot, holding burns in place and slowly widens the flame, and dragging while pressed burns a path; hovering no longer burns
A quick click always gets a short guaranteed burn (240ms) so taps light reliably, even a press made while the sheet is loading or breaking
The flame widens only while you hold it still, so a pressed drag keeps a steady stroke width instead of fattening the longer you hold
Hovering keeps a quieter flame cursor as a pilot light showing where a press would burn, and still fans the fire lightly; the idle-ember timer is gone
Each press gets its own flame and a new press evicts the faintest fading flame, so rapid clicks never run out of flame slots; a mouse drag that starts outside the cover lights on entry, and a missed release is caught on the next move so a flame can never stay stuck on
When the sheet lets go it now breaks along the burn itself: the burn field is read back once at break time as a mask, connected regions of remaining paper are labelled, and each island flies off as one piece with its true shape
Paper still joined stays one piece, so a sheet with holes but no cut-through falls as one sheet, and only burnt-through gaps separate pieces
The mask matches the visible holes exactly (same frayed edge and threshold as the display), uses strict side-by-side connectivity, and labels are grown two texels into the holes so piece edges keep their full ember lip
Pieces are masked per pixel by a label texture with smoothed membership, so a bridge too thin for the mask snaps with a soft char line and a brief ember flash instead of a blocky edge
Islands under 24 texels become ash flecks that rise, turn grey and shrink away; single-texel specks are dropped, and at most 96 pieces fly per sheet
Flight scales with island size: big pieces lift less, sway slower, rock and spin less, drag more, rarely flip, lift a beat later and recede as they fall, while small pieces flutter and tumble faster
Pieces fade out by the true lowest edge of their rotated outline, so large pieces dissolve before reaching the canvas edge instead of being clipped
The sim freezes for the frame or two the async readback takes so the pieces match the exact moment of the break; the readback uses a pixel buffer and fence and runs only at break time
The random Voronoi crack grid and its seeds are gone; the label textures, mask target and readback buffer are disposed with the engine
Copy and accessible label updated to say press and drag to burn

Paper near the burn now curls up and away from the heat: a height field from the blurred burn and heat lifts the sheet along the char edge, pulls the edge back a few pixels and shades the bend with a lit side and a shadowed side
The lifted char edge casts a soft shadow onto the next cover showing through the hole
Falling pieces are now bent 3D sheets: each one is an instanced 10x10 grid that curls along one axis like a cylinder, with a gentle travelling wave across it, drawn in one call
Curl starts flat at the break so nothing pops, then grows as the piece cools, faster for hot pieces; a few curl the other way
Big pieces curl slowly and only a little with a broad gentle wave, small pieces curl tightly and flutter their curl quickly, flecks roll up tightest
Pieces tumble in real 3D: the old flat squash is now a rotation about an in-plane axis plus a second smaller wobble about the cross axis, on top of the existing spin, with perspective foreshortening so near edges grow and far edges shrink
Surface normals drive the shading on both faces, so folds and twists light and darken as they turn, with a slight darkening at grazing angles; the back face still shows the browned paper back
Curled pieces draw their hollow side before their outer side, so a piece that curls over itself layers correctly without a depth buffer
The fall-out fade measures the lowest edge from the full 3D rotation with a margin for perspective
Reduced motion keeps pieces flat with no curl or tumble and fades them in place as before

Detachment is now physical: the sheet hangs from its top edge and any island of paper no longer joined to it through unburnt paper drops away on its own, the moment it is cut free
Removed the global break (36% burnt, or cold past 24% for 1.6s); paper still joined to the top edge stays put and keeps burning, so you can cut one piece out and watch only that piece fall
While anything is burning, a 128 by 128 burn mask is read back about six times a second through a pixel buffer and fence, never stalling a frame; labelling the islands takes about 0.6ms on the CPU
Each detached island is handed over the same frame it appears: its cells are written into the sheet's label texture, a snapshot of just those pixels is drawn for the fragment, and the live sheet masks the same cells with the same smoothed membership the fragment uses, so the hole and the piece line up with no double image
Detached paper is frozen in the simulation and insulated from its neighbours, so a fallen piece keeps its ember while it flies but can no longer pass heat back into the sheet
Cut pieces lift within about a tenth of a second; the final drop of a sheet still staggers its pieces from the burn outward
The next sheet takes over only when less than 10% of the paper is still attached, or on Next sheet, and either way the remaining paper falls as its true pieces
The burn counter now reads % gone, the share of the sheet that has burnt through or fallen
The sheet underneath is protected: it takes no glow or soot through the holes, heat dropped over a hole is damped to 40% so at most it warms the edge of the paper left, and a flame still held when a sheet changes goes out until you lift and press again
Islands beyond the 96-fragment cap evict the oldest ash flecks first; specks under two mask cells turn to ash with no fragment
Detach sounds scale with the size of the piece, with the full whoosh kept for a sheet's final drop
Album covers are gone: the deck is now seven real photographs already in the repo (alpine valley, wildflower meadow, light beams at night, reading in the field, a visitor over the daisies, the clock tower, sitting on the wires), loaded same-origin, decoded before upload and cycled as each is used up
Each photo is presented as a print: centre-cropped to square with the subject kept, set inside a thin warm-white border, and upscaled smoothly with high-quality canvas filtering and no sharpening
Dark areas still burn faster: fuel comes from each photo's own luminance and colour, levelled per print as it was with the covers
The next photos are fetched and decoded while one burns, and a photo that is still loading fades in under the holes instead of popping
The Spotify loading in page.js and the covers module are removed, and the brief procedural paper sheets are dropped in favour of the photos
